name: Lower Egypt
alt: Northern kingdom of the First Intermediate Period

predecessors.name: Old Kingdom of Egypt
predecessors.text: the Delta and Middle Egypt south to Siut, the northern part of the Old Kingdom

successors.name: Middle Kingdom of Egypt
successors.text: the Heracleopolitan kingdom, conquered by the Theban Mentuhotep II

ledger.x: c. 2181 BC: the Old Kingdom ends and the Memphite Seventh and Eighth Dynasties rule the north. Infobox 'Memphis (c. 2181 BC - c. 2160 BC), Seventh Dynasty-Eighth Dynasty'; the period 'spanned approximately 125 years, c. 2181 - c. 2055 BC'. The page names the capital, not the land; the Lower Egypt shape is Cliopatria's.

c. 2160 BC: the Ninth Dynasty takes over at Heracleopolis Magna. Infobox 'Heracleopolis Magna (c. 2160 BC - c. 2050 BC), Ninth Dynasty-Tenth Dynasty'; 'Akhthoes was described as a king who caused much harm to the inhabitants of Egypt'.
c. 2160 BC: the capital moves from Memphis to Heracleopolis Magna (Ihnasya el-Medina), in Lower Egypt.

c. 2069 BC: Thebes attacks the Abydos region. The page dates no assault: 'Intef II begins the assault on the north, particularly at Abydos'; the year is the start of Intef III's reign in the infobox ('c. 2069 BC - c. 2061 BC: Intef III'), who 'completed the conquest of Abydos'.
c. 2061 BC: the Abydos fighting ends in a Theban victory (Thebes 'c. 2134 BC - c. 2061 BC').

c. 2061 BC: Intef III takes Abydos from the Heracleopolitans. Page: 'His successor, Intef III, completed the conquest of Abydos, moving into Middle Egypt against the Heracleopolitan kings.' Undated; placed at the end of the Theban Eleventh Dynasty's c. 2061 BC date. Siut stays northern: it 'acted as a buffer state'.

c. 2055 BC: Mentuhotep II's war against Heracleopolis begins on the Siut borderland. The page dates no campaign of his; the year is his accession in the Middle Kingdom page (2055 BC), after Intef III had 'moved into Middle Egypt'.
c. 2033 BC: the war ends with Mentuhotep II's victory 'around 2033 BC'.

c. 2033 BC: Mentuhotep II defeats the Heracleopolitan kings and Egypt is reunited. Page: he 'would eventually defeat the Heracleopolitan kings around 2033 BC and unify the country. This event marked the beginning of the Middle Kingdom of Egypt.' The Middle Kingdom page instead puts his accession in 2055 BC.
c. 2033 BC: the northern kingdom ends with the Theban conquest.

wars.name: Theban-Heracleopolitan war
wars.outcome: The Theban Eleventh Dynasty took Abydos (Intef III) and 'moving into Middle Egypt'; Mentuhotep II 'would eventually defeat the Heracleopolitan kings around 2033 BC and unify the country'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey borders; the northern kingdom is Cliopatria's Delta-and-Middle-Egypt shape, with the Siut buffer in the south (page) and Abydos disputed from c.
